issues.legal_issue: The security-taking procedure for disputed succession claims does not apply when an intestate estate is transmissible to one heir and competing claimants each assert that they are that sole heir.
material_facts: The estate owner died intestate, and the estate was claimed as a whole by persons each asserting sole-heir status.
One claimant was in possession of the estate, while another claimant, out of possession, had brought a title suit and sought security from the possessor pending its decision.
issues.conclusion: The provision for taking security did not apply to a dispute in which the deceased left only one heir entitled to the entire estate; the appeal was allowed and the application for security was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The court treated the Bengal Wills and Intestacy Regulation V of 1799 as restrictive legislation to be strictly construed. It held that sections II, III, and IV were complete provisions for distinct situations: a testate estate with an executor, an intestate estate with a single heir, and an intestate estate with more than one heir, respectively. The security procedure in section IV therefore applied to the multiple-heir situation, not to a dispute between rival claimants each asserting sole heirship in a single-heir estate. The court distinguished Cohen v. S.E. Railway (1877) 2 E. & D. 253 and considered the related treatment of joint succession in Regulation XI of 1793.

rule.if: security_application_in_succession_dispute and intestate_decedent and single_heir_estate and rival_claimants_each_assert_sole_heirship

predicates.security_application_in_succession_dispu: An out-of-possession claimant sought security from a person in possession while a succession title dispute was pending.
predicates.intestate_decedent: The person whose estate was claimed died without leaving a will.
predicates.single_heir_estate: The applicable succession arrangement provided for one heir to take the entire estate.
predicates.rival_claimants_each_assert_sole_heirshi: Two or more claimants disputed succession, each asserting that they alone were entitled to the entire estate.

issues.definition: When an out-of-possession claimant seeks security in an intestate succession dispute involving an estate transmissible to one heir and rival claims of sole heirship, the security-taking power does not apply.
